config.title: Search systems

intro.title: Search systems
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple search system that allows users to query a dataset and receive relevant results. You will learn the core concept of implementing a basic search algorithm, focusing on keyword matching and result ranking. The main technologies involved include data structures for storing information and functions to process search queries. By the end, you will understand how search systems work at a fundamental level and be able to create your own basic search functionality.
intro.usecase: Search systems are a foundational component of nearly every modern digital product. They power the core user experience in e-commerce sites like Amazon, content platforms like YouTube, and productivity tools like Slack, where users rely on fast, relevant results to find products, videos, or messages. As a developer, you'll implement these systems to handle features such as autocomplete suggestions, filtering dashboards, or document retrieval, ensuring scalability and performance under heavy user traffic.

objectives: Construct a basic search system architecture with indexing and query components
Implement an inverted index data structure to map terms to document IDs
Configure a tokenizer to process raw text into searchable terms
Apply a ranking algorithm to sort search results by relevance
Integrate a query parser to handle user search input
Manulate search parameters to control result filtering and pagination
Initialize a search system with sample data and validate its functionality

steps.title: Define the core search system components
steps.instruction: Create a conceptual description of the three main components of a search system: Query Processor, Indexer, and Ranking Algorithm.
steps.hint: Think about what each component does in a search system. The Query Processor handles user queries, the Indexer organizes data for fast retrieval, and the Ranking Algorithm determines result relevance.

successCriteria: The description includes all three components: Query Processor, Indexer, and Ranking Algorithm with their basic functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Design the data model for searchable items
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'SearchableItem' with properties that represent a searchable document. Include at least: id (string), title (string), content (string), and tags (string[]).
steps.hint: Think about what information a search system needs to index and retrieve. The interface should describe the shape of each item in your search index.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a clear data model that defines what properties each searchable item must have, which is essential for building the indexer and query processor.
successCriteria: The SearchableItem interface is defined with id (string), title (string), content (string), and tags (string[]) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your interface includes all required properties: id (string), title (string), content (string), and tags (string[]).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Please define a TypeScript interface named 'SearchableItem' with the specified properties.

steps.title: Create the search index structure
steps.instruction: Design an inverted index structure by creating a function named `createInvertedIndex` that takes an array of searchable items and returns a mapping of terms to document IDs.
steps.hint: Think about how you would organize words from item titles/descriptions to quickly find which documents contain them.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that processes searchable items and builds an index where each term points to the IDs of documents containing that term.
successCriteria: The createInvertedIndex function is defined and returns an object mapping terms to arrays of document IDs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function processes all items and builds a proper term-to-document-ID mapping.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inverted index structure isn't quite right. Review how search indexes map terms to document IDs for efficient lookup.

steps.title: Implement the indexing function
steps.instruction: Implement the createInvertedIndex function to tokenize text from items and build an inverted index mapping terms to document IDs.
steps.hint: Loop through each item, split its content into words (tokens), and add the item's ID to the set for each token in the index object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createInvertedIndex function will process an array of items and return an inverted index object where each term points to an array of document IDs containing that term.
successCriteria: The createInvertedIndex function is implemented with tokenization logic and returns an index object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function loops through items, tokenizes the content, and adds each item's ID to the corresponding term's array in the index object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match the requirements. Review how to tokenize text and build an inverted index mapping terms to document IDs.

steps.title: Design the query processing logic
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'processQuery' that takes a search query string as input and returns an array of normalized tokens.
steps.hint: The function should split the query into individual words and convert them to lowercase for consistency.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that processes search queries by tokenizing and normalizing them.
successCriteria: The 'processQuery' function is defined, takes a string parameter, and returns an array of lowercase tokens.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes a query string as input and returns an array of normalized tokens (lowercase).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating a function that processes search queries. It should accept a string and return an array of tokens after splitting and converting to lowercase.

steps.title: Implement the search matching algorithm
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'searchDocuments' that takes a query string and the inverted index, and returns an array of document IDs that match the query terms.
steps.hint: Think about splitting the query into terms, looking up each term in the inverted index, and combining the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that can find documents containing specific search terms using the inverted index structure.
successCriteria: The searchDocuments function is defined, takes query and index parameters, splits the query into terms, looks up terms in the index, and returns an array of matching document IDs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly splits the query into terms and looks them up in the inverted index to find matching document IDs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The searchDocuments function should take a query and index, process the query terms, and return matching document IDs from the index. Try implementing the basic matching logic.

steps.title: Design the ranking system
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'calculateRelevanceScore' that takes a document and a query term as parameters and returns a numeric score based on term frequency.
steps.hint: Think about how often the query term appears in the document. You can start with a simple scoring approach.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named calculateRelevanceScore is defined that takes a document and query term and returns a numeric score.
successCriteria: The calculateRelevanceScore function is defined with two parameters and returns a number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'calculateRelevanceScore' and returns a numeric value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name, parameters, and ensure it returns a number.

steps.title: Implement the ranking function
steps.instruction: Create a function named rankSearchResults that takes search results and relevance scores,
steps.hint: The function should accept an array of search results and an array of relevance scores, combine them, sort by score, and return the sorted results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A rankSearchResults function that sorts search results by relevance score.
successCriteria: The rankSearchResults function is defined, accepts results and scores arrays, combines them, sorts by score descending, and returns sorted results.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the ranking function. Make sure it accepts both results and scores, combines them, sorts by score descending, and returns the sorted results.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ranking function is missing or doesn't properly sort results by relevance score. Review the function requirements.

steps.title: Test the complete search system
steps.instruction: Create a test function named testSearchSystem that indexes sample documents and verifies search queries return correct results.
steps.hint: Define a function that creates test data, calls your existing functions (createInvertedIndex, search), and logs or returns the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function is created that validates the end-to-end search functionality with sample data.
successCriteria: The testSearchSystem function is defined and includes calls to index documents and verify search queries.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the test function. Make sure it includes both indexing and query verification steps.
